questions.q: Two persons $A$ and $B$ are located in $X-Y$ plane at the points $(0,0)$ and $(0,10)$ respectively. (The distances are measured in MKS unit). At a time $t=0$, they start moving simultaneously with velocities $\quad \overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}_A=2 \mathbf{j} \mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1} \quad$ and $\quad \overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}_B=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}} \mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ respectively. The time after which $A$ and $B$ are at their closest distance is
questions.solution:
Let after the time $(t)$ the position of $A$ is \left(0, v_A t\right)$ and position of $B= \left(v_B t, 10\right)$. Distance between them
\begin{aligned}$y & $=\sqrt{\left(0-v_B t\right)^2+\left(v_A t-10\right)^2}$\\ \text { or } \quad y^2 & =(2 t)^2+(2 t-10)^2\end{aligned}$ or $\quad y^2=l=4 t^2+4 t^2+100-40 t\Rightarrow \quad l=8 t^2+100-40 t$ Now, $\quad $\frac{d l}{d t}=($16 $t-40)=0t=\frac{40}{16}=$2.5 \mathrm{~s}$ As \frac{d^2 l}{d t^2}=$16=(+\mathrm{ve})$ Hence, $l$ will be minimum.$

questions.q: The displacement $x$ of a particle varies with time $t$ as $x = ae^{- \alphat} + be^{\betat}$, where $a, b, \alpha$ and $\beta$ are positive constants. The velocity of the particle will
questions.solution:
$x = ae^{- \alphat} + be^{\betat}$
$\dfrac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} = - a\alphae^{- \alphat} + \text{b}\betae^{\betat}$
$⇒ v = \text{b}\betae^{\betat} - a\alphae^{- \alphat}$
As $t$ increases, $e^{- \alphat}$ decreases and $e^{\betat}$ increases.
So $v$ will increase with time.

questions.q: A police party is moving in a jeep at a constant speed $v$. They saw a thief at a distance $x$ on a motorcycle which is at rest. The moment the police saw the thief, the thief started at constant acceleration $a$. Which of the following relations is true if the police is able to catch the thief?
questions.solution:
Let the police party catch the thief after $t$ second. $\therefore$ Distance travelled by police party in $t$ second $=v t$ and distance travelled by thief $=x+\frac{1}{2} \alpha t^2$
So, $\quad x+\frac{1}{2} \alpha t^2 \leq v t$ or $\quad \frac{\alpha t^2}{2}-v t+x=0$ or $\quad t=\frac{v \pm \sqrt{v^2-2 \alpha x}}{\alpha}$ For $t$ to be real, $v^2 \geq 2 \alpha x$

questions.q: A car accelerates from rest with $2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ on a straight line path and then comes to rest after applying brakes. Total distance travelled by the car is $100 \mathrm{~m}$ in 20 seconds. Then, the maximum velocity attained by the car is
questions.solution:
Given,
Acceleration of $\operatorname{car}(\alpha)=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$
Distance covered by car in 20 seconds $(s)=100 \mathrm{~m}$
We know that, $\begin{aligned}$s & =$\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\alpha \beta}{\alpha+\beta}$t^2 \\
100 & =$\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2 \beta}{(2+\beta)} \times$20 $\times$20 \\
$\frac{100}{400}$& =$\frac{\beta}{(2+\beta)}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{1}{4}$& =$\frac{\beta}{2+\beta}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad 4 $\beta$& =2+$\beta$\\
\Rightarrow \quad 3 $\beta$& =2 \Rightarrow $\text { retardation } \beta=\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^2 \\
& \therefore \quad $\text { Maximum velocity }\left($v_{\text {max }}\right)=$\frac{\alpha \beta t}{\alpha+\beta}
\end{aligned} \begin{aligned}$& =$\frac{2 \times \frac{2}{3} \times 20}{2+\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{\frac{80}{3}}{\frac{8}{3}}=\frac{80}{3} \times \frac{3}{8}$\\
& =10 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}

questions.q: Ball-1 is dropped from the top of a building from rest. At the same moment, ball- 2 is thrown upward towards ball-l with a speed $14 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ from a point $21 \mathrm{~m}$ below the top of building. How far will the ball-1 have dropped when it passes ball-2. (Assume, acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$.)
questions.solution:
Suppose that both the balls meet at a distance $h$ from ball-l after time $t$ from the start as shown in the figure, For downward motion of ball-1, from second equation of the motion, $\begin{aligned}$& h=u t+$\frac{1}{2}$g t² \\ & h=0 $\times$t+$\frac{1}{2} \times$10 t² \quad \ldots(i) \\ & h=5 t² \quad[\because u=0] \end{aligned}
For upward motion of ball-2, from second equation of the motion, h=v t-$\frac{1}{2}$g t² Given, speed of ball-2,v $=14 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ Substituting these values in Eq. (iii), we get $\begin{aligned}$& 21-h=14 t-$\frac{1}{2} \times$10 t² \\ \Rightarrow \quad & 21-h=14 t-5 t² \end{aligned} Adding Eq. (ii) and (iv), we get $\begin{aligned}$& 21=14 t \\ & \Rightarrow \quad t=$\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{~s}=$1.5 $\mathrm{~s}$\\ & \end{aligned} $\therefore$ From Eq. (ii), we get $\begin{aligned}$h & =5 $\times($1.5)^2=11.25 $\mathrm{~m}$\\ & =$\frac{45}{4} \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned}$Therefore, the ball-l will have dropped $\frac{45}{4} \mathrm{~m}$ when it passes ball-2.

questions.q: A vehicle starts moving in a straight line with an acceleration, $a=4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$, with initial velocity equal to zero. After accelerating for time $t_1$, the vehicle moves uniformly and for time $t_2$, the vehicle finally decelerates for time $t_1$ eventually coming to a stop. The total time taken during the motion is $10 \mathrm{~s}$ and the average velocity during the motion is $5.1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The time taken by the vehicle during acceleration is
questions.solution: For first part of journey, $x=0, a=4 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$, time $=t_1$. Velocity attained by particle at end of time $t_1$ is $\quad v_1=u+a t_1=4 t_1\therefore$ Displacement in first $t_1$ seconds is s_1=$\frac{1}{2}$a t_1^2=$\frac{1}{2} \times$4 $\times$t_1^2=2 t_1^2 For second part of journey, initial velocity, $v_1=4 t_1$, time $=t_2$ and acceleration $=0$. $\therefore$ Displacement in next $t_2$ seconds is $s_2=v_1 t_2=4 t_1 t_2$ For third part of journey, Initial velocity, $v_1=4 t_1$ Final velocity $=0$ Time interval $=t_1$ So, acceleration $=\frac{0-4 t_1}{t_1}=-4 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\therefore$ Displacement in third part is s_3=$\frac{-16 t_1^2}{-8}=$2 t_1^2 \quad\left(\because$v_2^2-v_1^2=2 a s_3\right) Now, $\quad v_{\text {avg }}=\frac{\text { Total displacement }}{\text { Total time }}\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } 5.1=$\frac{s_1+s_2+s_3}{t_1+t_2+t_1}$\\ \text{ and } {\left[\therefore \text { third time interva] }=$t_1\right]} \\ & 5.1=$\frac{2 t_1^2+4 t_1 t_2+2 t_1^2}{10} \end{aligned} \begin{array}{lc} \Rightarrow$& 5 $\mathrm{l}=$4 t_1^2+4 t_1\left($10-2 t_1\right) \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } 5 $\mathrm{l}=$4 t_1^2+40 t_1-8 t_1^2 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } 4 t_1^2-40 t_1+5 $\mathrm{l}=$0 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } 4 t_1^2-34 t_1-6 t_1+5 $\mathrm{l}=$0 \end{array} $\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \quad\left($2 t_1-3\right)\left($2 t_1-17\right)=0 \Rightarrow t_1=$\frac{3}{2}$\\ \text{ and } $\text { or }$\\ \text{ and } t_1=$\frac{17}{2} \Rightarrow$t_1=1.5 $\mathrm{~s}$\\ \text{ and } \end{aligned} (As $t_1=8.5 \mathrm{~s}$ is not possible. It exceeds total time.)$

questions.q: A particle starts from rest and traverses a distance $2x$ with uniform acceleration, then moves uniformly over a further distance $4x$ and finally comes to rest after moving a further distance $6x$ under uniform retardation. Assuming entire motion to be rectilinear motion, the ratio of average speed over the journey to the maximum speed on its way is
questions.solution:
Let ${t}_{1}$,${t}_{2}$ and ${t}_{3}$ be the time taken by the particles to cover the distance $2x$, $4x$ and $6x$ respectively. Let $v$ be the velocity of the particle at $Bie$, maximum velocity. The particle moves with uniform acceleration from $A$ to $B$.

For motion from $A$ to $B$.

Average velocity $= \dfrac{0 + v}{2} = \dfrac{v}{2}$

Time taken, ${t}_{1} = \dfrac{2x}{\dfrac{v}{2}}$

Particle moves with uniform retardation from $C$ TO $D$, ${V}_{avg} = \dfrac{0 + v}{2} = \dfrac{v}{2}$

Time taken ,${t}_{3} = \dfrac{6x}{( \dfrac{v}{2} )}$

Total time $= {t}_{1} + {t}_{2} + {t}_{3}$

$t = \dfrac{2x}{v2} + \dfrac{4x}{v} + \dfrac{6x}{v2} = \dfrac{20x}{v}$

Average Velocity over $= \dfrac{6x + 2x + 4x}{\dfrac{20x}{v}} = \dfrac{3}{5}v$

Required Ratio $= \dfrac{Average Speed}{v} = \dfrac{3}{5}$

questions.q: A bullet emerges from a barrel of length $1 . 2m$ with a speed of $640ms^{- 1}$. Assuming constant acceleration, the approximate time that is spent in the barrel after the gun is fired is
questions.solution:
Given, $s = 1.2m, v = 640\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}, a = ? , u = 0; t = ?$

We have the third equation of motion

$2as = v^{2} - u^{2}$

$2a \times 1.2 = 640 \times 640$

Or $a = \dfrac{8 \times 64 \times {10}^{3}}{3}$

And by first equation of motion

$v = u + at$

Or $t = \dfrac{v}{a} = \dfrac{15}{4} \times {10}^{- 3}$

$= 3.75 \times {10}^{- 3}s \approx 4ms$

questions.q:
A body covers first $\dfrac{1}{3}$ part of its journey with a velocity of $2ms^{- 1}$, next $\dfrac{1}{3}$ part with a velocity of $3ms^{- 1}$ and~the rest of the journey with a velocity $6ms^{- 1} .$& The average velocity of the body will be&
&
questions.solution:
Let the total distance be& $3xm .$

For first $\dfrac{1}{3}rd$~distance~$xm,$~let~ time~be& ${t}_{1}$.

$∵ time = \dfrac{distance}{speed}$

$∴ {t}_{1} = \dfrac{x}{2}s. . . ( i )$

For second~$\dfrac{1}{3}rd$ distance $xm,$~let time~be~${t}_{2}$.~

$∵ time = \dfrac{distance}{speed}$

$∴ {t}_{2} = \dfrac{x}{3}s$~$. . . ( ii )$

and for third~$\dfrac{1}{3}rd$~distance~$xm,$~let time~be~${t}_{3} .$

$⇒ {t}_{3} = \dfrac{x}{6}$~ $. . . ( iii )$

$∴$~Average velocity~for entire~journey.

${v}_{av} = \dfrac{totaldisplacement}{totaltime}$

$⇒ {v}_{av} = \dfrac{3x}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2} + {t}_{3}}$

$= \dfrac{3x}{\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{x}{3} + \dfrac{x}{6}}$~ ~

$= \dfrac{3x}{x\left(\dfrac{3 + 2 + 1}{6}\right)} = 3ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A truck of mass $\mathrm{M}$ and a car of mass $\frac{\mathrm{M}}{10}$ moving with same momentum are brought to halt by the application of same breaking force. The ratio of the distances travelled by truck and car before they come to stop is
questions.solution: Mass of truck, $m_1=M$ Mass of car, $m_2=\frac{M}{10}$ Initial velocity of truck $=u_1$ Initial velocity of $c a r=u_2$ Momentum of car \& truck are same thus, $\begin{aligned}$& $\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{T}}=\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{C}}$\\ & $\mathrm{m}}_{1} \mathrm{u}}_{1}=$\mathrm{m}}_{2} \mathrm{u}}_{2} \\ & $\mathrm{M} \mathrm{u}}_{1}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{M}}{10}\right) \mathrm{u}}_{2} \\  \text{ and }  \therefore $\frac{\mathrm{u}_1}{\mathrm{u}_2}=\frac{1}{10} \end{aligned}$Both car \ \text{ and }  truck will come to rest, thus their final velocity is zero. using $\mathrm{eq}^{\mathrm{n}}$ of motion, $\mathrm{v}^2-\mathrm{u}^2=2$ as Rearranging, put $\mathrm{v}=0 \ \text{ and } \mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{m}}\mathrm{S}=-\frac{\mathrm{mu}^2}{2 \mathrm{~F}}$Ratio of distance travelled by truck \ \text{ and }  car is given as $\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and }  $\frac{\mathrm{S}_1}{\mathrm{~S}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_1 \mathrm{u}_1^2}{2 \mathrm{~F}} \times \frac{2 \mathrm{~F}}{\mathrm{~m}_2 \mathrm{u}_2^2}=\frac{\mathrm{p}_1(2 \mathrm{~F}) \mathrm{u}_1}{\left(\mathrm{p}_2\right)(2 \mathrm{~F}) \mathrm{u}_2}$\\  \text{ and }  $\text { since, } \mathrm{p}}_{1}= \mathrm{p}}_{2} \\ & $\frac{\mathrm{S}_1}{\mathrm{~S}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{u}_1}{\mathrm{u}_2}=\frac{1}{10} \end{aligned}$

if~${t}_{2}$~is the time taken by the ball to hit the ground,

questions.q: A bus moving on a level road with a velocity $v$ can be stopped at a distance of $x$, by the application of a retarding force $F$. The load on the bus is increased by $25 \%$ by boarding the passengers. Now, if the bus is moving with the same speed and if the same retarding force is applied, the distance travelled by the bus before it stops is
questions.solution: By third's law of motion $v^2=u^2+2 a s\begin{aligned} v^2-u^2 & =-2\left(\frac{F}{m}\right) \cdot s \\ -u^2 & =-2 \frac{F}{m} \cdot s \\ u^2 & =\frac{2 F \cdot s}{m} \\ \text { or } \quad m & =\frac{2 F \cdot s}{u^2} \Rightarrow m \propto s \end{aligned}$ Given $s_1=x\begin{aligned} s_2 & =? \\ m_1 & =m \\ m_2 & =m \times 25 \%+m \end{aligned}$ Now, $\quad \frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{s_1}{s_2}\begin{array}{ll} \frac{m}{m \times \frac{25}{100}+m} =\frac{x}{s_2}\\ s_2 =\frac{x \times m\left(\frac{100+25}{100}\right)}{m}\\ s_2 =\frac{125}{100}x \\ s_2 =1.25 x \end{array}$

questions.solution: When ball is at maximum height, its velocity is zero. From first equation of motion, $v=u-g t \Rightarrow 0=u-10 \times 5 \Rightarrow u=50 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Distance travelled in $n$th second, $s_n=u+\frac{a}{2}(2 n-1)$ Distance travelled in 2nd second is given as $s_2=50-\frac{10}{2}(4-1)=50-15=35 \mathrm{~m}$ Distance travelled in 7th second is equal to distance travelled in 2nd second from highest point to vertically downward direction. $s_7=s_2{ }^{\prime}=0+\frac{10}{2}(2 \times 2-1)=15 \mathrm{~m}\therefore \quad \frac{s_2}{s_7}=\frac{s_2}{s_2{ }^{\prime}}=\frac{35}{15}=\frac{7}{3}$ or $7: 23$

questions.solution:
The object initially at rest at origin begins to move in the& $+ x$~direction, thus at~$x = 0$,~$u = 0$.

Applying the second equation of motion,~$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2} .$

Putting the values, we get~$x = \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$. Thus, from~$t = 0$~to~$4s$, the graph will be parabolic.

Now, the object moves with a uniform acceleration~$a = 1ms^{- 2}$~for~$t = 4s$.

$x = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times {4}^{2} = 8m$.

After that, it moves with uniform velocity~$v = 4ms^{- 1}$.

We know that~$v = \dfrac{d x}{d t} = 4$

Integrating the above equation,${∫}_{0}^{8} d x = {∫}_{4}^{t}4 d t$

$x - 8 = 4\left(t - 4\right) ⇒ x = 4t - 8$

The above equation represents the equation of a straight line.

Hence, the graph will be

questions.q: Two towns $A$ and $B$ are connected by a regular bus service with a bus leaving in either direction every $T$ min. A man cycling with a speed of $20 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ from $A$ to $B$ notices that a bus travelling in the direction of his motion goes past him every $18 \mathrm{~min}$ and every $6 \mathrm{~min}$ he notices a bus travelling in the opposite direction go past him. Assuming that, the buses travel with a constant speed. Find $T$ and the constant speed of the buses.
questions.solution: Let, the speed of bus be $v_B$ and that of cyclist be $v_C$. Case 1 Bus moving from $A$ to $B$, Relative speed of bus $=v_B-v_C=v_B-20$ Distance covered $=$ Velocity $\times$ Time d=\left(v_B-20\right) \times 18...(i) Case 2 Bus moving from $B$ to $A$, Relative speed of bus $=v_B+v_C$ =v_B+20 Distance covered $=$ Velocity $\times$ Time d=\left(v_B+20\right) \times 6...(ii) From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $\begin{aligned}$& \left(v_B-20\right) \times 18=\left(v_B+20\right) \times 6 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad v_B=40 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h} \\ & \text { From Eq. (ii), }\left(v_B+20\right) \times 6=v_B \times T \\ & \Rightarrow \quad(40+20) \times 6=40 \times T \\ & \Rightarrow \quad T=9 \min $=\frac{9}{60} \mathrm{~h}=\frac{3}{20} \mathrm{~h} .$\\ & \end{aligned}

questions.q: A particle is moving along $X$-axis with velocity $v=e^{-\beta x}$. At time $t=0$, the particle is located at $x=0$. The displacement of the particle as function of time is
questions.solution:
Velocity of particle, $v=e^{-\beta x}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x}{d t}=e^{-\beta x}$ or $\quad \frac{d x}{e^{-\beta x}}=d t$ or $\quad e^{\beta x} d x=d t$
⇒ Integrating, we get $\int_0^x e^{\beta x} d x=\int_0^t d t\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\beta}\left[e^{\beta x}\right]_0^x=[t]_0^t \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{\beta}\left(e^{\beta x}-e^0\right)=t-0 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\beta}\left(e^{\beta x}-1\right)=t\end{aligned}e^{\beta x}=\beta t+1$ Taking log, we get $\log \left(e^{\beta x}\right)=\log (\beta t+1)\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & \beta x=\log (\beta t+1) \\ \Rightarrow & x=\frac{1}{\beta} \cdot \log (\beta t+1)\end{array} So, displacement function for the particle is $x=$\frac{1}{\beta} \cdot \log (\beta$t+1)

questions.q: A particle moving in a straight line covers half the distance with a speed of & $3ms^{- 1}$. The other half of the distance is covered in two equal time intervals with speeds of $4.5ms^{- 1}$and $7 . 5ms^{- 1}$. The average speed of the particle during this motion is
questions.solution:
Let total distance be& $S$~and~time required to cover~first half is& ${t}_{1}$~and second half is~$2{t}_{2}$.

Since~$\text{Time=}\dfrac{Distance}{Speed}$

~Given,

${t}_{1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{S}{2}}{3} = \dfrac{S}{6}, {t}_{2} = \dfrac{S1}{4 . 5} = \dfrac{S2}{7 . 5}$

From the given data, we know that~${S}_{1} + {S}_{2} = \dfrac{S}{2}$

$⇒ 4 . 5{t}_{2} + 7 . 5{t}_{2} = \dfrac{S}{2}$

$⇒ {t}_{2} = \dfrac{S}{24}$

Average speed~$= \dfrac{S}{{t}_{1} + 2{t}_{2}} = = \dfrac{S}{\dfrac{S}{6} + \dfrac{2S}{24}} = 4ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: At time $t=0$, a particle leaves the origin and moves in the positive direction of the $X$-axis. If the velocity of the particles varies as $\mathbf{v}(t)=\mathbf{v}_0\left(1-\frac{t}{t_0}\right),\left|\mathbf{v}_0\right|=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $t_0=10 \mathrm{~s}$, then the distance covered by the particle during the first $20 \mathrm{~s}$ is
questions.solution: Given that, At $t=0, x=0$ and $u=\mathbf{v}=-\mathbf{v}_0$ At any time $t$, velocity of particle, \mathbf{v}=\mathbf{v}_0\left($1-$\frac{t}{t_0}\right)=\mathbf{v}_0-$\frac{\mathbf{v}_0}{t_0}$t Velocity will become zero at time $t_1\begin{array}{ll} \therefore$ \text{ and } 0=\mathbf{v}_0-$\frac{\mathbf{v}_0}{t_0}$t_1 \\ \Rightarrow \text{ and } t_1=$\frac{\mathbf{v}_0}{\mathbf{v}_0} \times$t_0=t_0=10 $\mathrm{~s} \end{array}\therefore$ For time interval from 0 to $10 \mathrm{~s}$, Acceleration, $\mathbf{a}_1=-\frac{\mathbf{v}_0}{t_0}=-\frac{10}{10}=-1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ and for time interval from 10 to $20 \mathrm{~s}$ Acceleration, $\mathbf{a}_2=\frac{\mathbf{v}_0}{t_0}=1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ Now, displacement in time 0 to $10 \mathrm{~s}\begin{aligned} \mathbf{s}_1=\mathbf{u} t_1+$\frac{1}{2} \mathbf{a}_1 \Rightarrow t_1^2 \text{ and } =\mathbf{v}_0(10)-$\frac{1}{2} \times$1(10)^2 \\ \text{ and } =10 $\times$10-50=50 $\mathrm{~m} \end{aligned}$and displacement for time $10 \mathrm{~s}$ to $20 \mathrm{~s}$, $\begin{aligned}$t_2 \text{ and } =20-10=10 $\mathrm{~s}$\\ \mathbf{s}_2=\mathbf{u} t+$\frac{1}{2} \mathbf{a}_2 t_2^2= \text{ and } 0+$\frac{1}{2} \times$1 $\times($10)^2 \\ \text{ and } =50 $\mathrm{~m}\left(\text { At }$t_1=10 $\mathrm{~s},$u_2=v=0\right) \end{aligned} Total distance travelled, $d=\left|s_1\right|+\left|s_2\right|=50+50=100 \mathrm{~m}

questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upward with an initial speed& $u$ from the top of a tower, reaches the ground with a speed $3u$. The height of the tower is:
questions.solution:
Let the height of the tower be& $h .$

Taking $+ ve$~$x -$axis along vertically upward direction, we have,

$u = u$

$a = - g$

$v = - 3u$

$s = AC = - h$

As acceleration remains constant.

Now using~$v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as,$~we get

$⇒ \left(-3u\right)2 = \left($u\right)2 + $2\left(-$g\right)\left(-h\right)$

$⇒ 9u^{2} = u^{2} + 2gh$

$⇒ 2gh = 8u^{2}$

$⇒ gh = 4u^{2}$

$⇒ h = $\dfrac{4u^{2}}{g}.

$

It's displacement after $2 \mathrm{~s}$ is

questions.q: A rocket is fired vertically from the ground with a resultant vertical acceleration of a \(10 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$\). Fuel is finished in \(1 $\mathrm{~min}$\) and it continues to move up. What is the maximum height reached ?
questions.solution: Resultant vertical acceleration, \(a=10 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$\) Height travelled by the rocket in \(1 $\mathrm{~min}($60 $\mathrm{~s})$\), \(\begin{aligned}h \text{ and } =u t+\frac{1}{2}a t² \\ \text{ and } =0 $\times$60+\frac{1}{2} \times10 $\times($60)^2 \\ \text{ and } =18000 $\mathrm{~m}=$18 $\mathrm{~km} \end{aligned}$\) Velocity of rocket after \(1 $\mathrm{~min}($60 $\mathrm{~s})$\), \(v=u+a t=0+10 $\times$60=600 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$\) After \(1 $\mathrm{~min}$\), when fuel of rocket is finished, then \(u=600 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1},$a=-g=-9.8 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^2\) Hence, if rocket goes at height \(h_2\), then \$(\begin{aligned}$v²-u² \text{ and } =2 g h_2 \\ 0-(600)^2 \text{ and } =2(-9.8) h_2 \\ \Rightarrow \quad h_2 \text{ and } =$\frac{360000}{2 \times 9.8}$\\ \text{ and } =18367.3 $\mathrm{~m}=$18.4 $\mathrm{~km} \end{aligned}$\) \(\therefore\) Maximum height travelled by rocket from ground \(=h_1+h_2=18+18.4=36.4 $\mathrm{~km}$\)

questions.q: A body travelling along a straight line path travels first half of the distance with a velocity \(7 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$\). During the travel time of the second half of the distance, first half time is travelled with a velocity \(14 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$\) and the second half time is travelled with a velocity \(21 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$\). Then the average velocity of the body during the journey is
questions.solution:
According to the question,
Given, a body travelling along a straight line path. Body travels first half of the distance \((A\) to \(B\)) with velocity, \(v_1=7 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}$\) Body travels second half of the distance ( \(B\) to \(C\)) in first half time with velocity, \(v_2=14 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}$\) and in the second half time with velocity, \(v_3=21 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}$\) Let the time taken to travelled from \(A\) to \(B=t\) second Now, distance covered from \(A\) to \(B=d_{A B}\) \(\therefore\) Distance, \(d=\) Velocity \($\times$\) Time \(\therefore \quad d_{A B}=7 t\)...(i) Now, distance covered from \(B\) to \(C=d_{B C}\) \(\therefore\) Average velocity of the body \(=$\frac{v_2+v_3}{2}$\) or \(\therefore \quad d_{B C}=v^{\prime} $\times$t^{\prime} \Rightarrow d_{B C}=$\frac{35}{2}$t^{\prime}\)...(ii) \(\therefore\) Distance travelled by the body from point \(A\) to \(B\) \(=\) distance travelled by the body from point \(B\) to \(C\). \(d_{A B}=d_{B C}\) From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get \(7 t=$\frac{35}{2}$t^{\prime} $\text { or }$t^{\prime}=$\frac{2}{5}$t\)...(iii) Now, the average velocity from \(A\) to \(C\), for finding distance \(d_{A C}\), \(v=$\frac{v_1+v_2+v_3}{3}=\frac{42}{3}=$14 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}$\)...(iv) \(\therefore\) Distance travelled from \(A\) to \(C\), \(\begin{aligned} \text{ and } d_{A C}=v $\times$t \\ \text{ and } $\text{or }$d_{A C}=14 t \quad $\text{...(v)[From Eq. (iv)]} \end{aligned}$\) Total time taken from \(A\) to \(C\), \$(\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } T=t+t^{\prime} \\ \text{ and } $\text{or }$T=t+$\frac{2 t}{5} \quad [\therefore \text{ From Eq. (iii)]}$\\ \text{ and } T=$\frac{7 t}{5} \quad \ldots ($vi) \end{aligned}\) Now, average velocity during the whole journey (From \(A\) to \(C\)), \(v_{\text {avg }}=$\frac{d_{A C}}{T} \text { or }$v_{\text {avg }}=$\frac{14 t}{7 t} \times$5\) [\(\therefore\) From Eqs. (v) and (vi)] or \(v_{\text {avg }}=10 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}$\)$

questions.solution: The position of the particle is given as $y(t)=10 t e^{-2 t}\ldots$ (i) Velocity of the particle is given as $v=\frac{d}{d t} y(t)=\frac{d}{d t}\left(10 t e^{-2 t}\right)=10\left[t e^{-2 t}(-2)+e^{-2 t} \cdot 1\right]=10\left[-2 t e^{-2 t}+e^{-2 t}\right]=10 e^{-2 t}(1-2 t)$ When body stops, then $v=0 \Rightarrow e^{-2 t}(1-2 t)=0 \Rightarrow 1-2 t=0t=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~s}\therefore$ From Eq. (i), displacement of the particle from origin is given as $y\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=10 \times \frac{1}{2} \times e^{-2 \times \frac{1}{2}}=5 e^{-1}=\frac{5}{e} \mathrm{~m}$

from Equation (1)

Futher, $\quad x^2+y^2=L^2$ [From the figure] Differentiating above equation w.r.t., time $t$, \therefore \quad 2 x $\frac{d x}{d t}+$2 y $\frac{d y}{d x}=$0 Now, putting the values of $\frac{d x}{d t}$ and $\frac{d y}{d t}$ from Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get \therefore \quad x v=y v^{\prime} $\text { or }$v^{\prime}=$\frac{x}{y}$v or $v^{\prime}=v \cot \theta$ [From the figure, $\because \cot \theta=\frac{x}{y}$ ] So, the downward velocity of the other end $B$ when the rod makes an angle $\theta$ with the floor is $v^{\prime}=v \cot \theta$

questions.q: A ball is thrown straight upward from ground with a speed of $20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The ball was caught on its way down at a point $5 \mathrm{~m}$ above the ground. The time taken by the ball during entire trip is (assume, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
The given situation of entire motion of ball is shown in the following figure.
Initial speed of ball, $u=20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Total time taken by the ball to reach at highest point $P$ is $t_1$, then from equation of vertical motion $v=u-g t \Rightarrow 0=20-10 t_1 \Rightarrow t_1=2 \mathrm{~s}$ Maximum height attained by the ball is $h$, then from equation $h=u t-\frac{1}{2} g t^2=20 \times 2-\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 2^2=40-20=20 \mathrm{~m}$ If $t_2$ be the time taken by the ball to reach at $B$ from point $P$, then $\begin{aligned} h-5 & =0 \times t_2+\frac{1}{2} g t_2^2 \Rightarrow 20-5=0+\frac{1}{2} \times 10 t_2^2 \\ 15 & =5 t_2^2 \Rightarrow t_2=\sqrt{3} \mathrm{~s} \end{aligned}\therefore$ Time taken by the ball during entire trip, $t=t_1+t_2=2+\sqrt{3} \mathrm{~s}$

questions.q: A motor-bike starts from rest, attains a velocity of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ with an acceleration of $0.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$, travels $10 \mathrm{~km}$ with this uniform velocity and then comes to halt with a uniform deceleration of $0.2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$. The total time of travel is
questions.solution:
The given situation of entire motion of motor bike is shown in the figure.
If time taken by the motorbike to reach from point $A$ to $B$ is $t_{A B}$, then for $A$ to $B$, $v_A=0, v_B=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}, a=0.5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\therefore$ From equation, $v=u+a t\begin{aligned} v_B & =v_A+a t_{A B} \Rightarrow 10=0+0.5 t_{A B} \\ \Rightarrow \quad t_{A B} & =\frac{10}{0.5}=20 \mathrm{~s} \end{aligned}$ Since, motorbike moves from point $B$ to $C$ with constant velocity. Hence, time taken to travel distance $B C$ is given as $t_{B C}=\frac{B C}{v_B}=\frac{10 \mathrm{~km}}{10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}}=\frac{10000 \mathrm{~m}}{10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}}=1000 \mathrm{~s}$ For motion of motorbike from point $C$ to $D$, time $=t_{C D}, v_B=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}, v_f=0, a^{\prime}=0.2 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ From equation, $v=u-a t$, $\begin{gathered} v_f=v_B-a^{\prime} t_{C D} \\ 0=10-0.2 \times t_{C D} \Rightarrow t_{C D}=50 \mathrm{~s} \\ \therefore \text { Total time }=t_{A B}+t_{B C}+t_{C D} \\ =20 \mathrm{~s}+1000 \mathrm{~s}+50 \mathrm{~s}=1070 \mathrm{~s} \end{gathered}$

questions.q: A car moving with a velocity \(6.25 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$\) is decelerated with \(2.5 $\sqrt{\mathrm{v}} \mathrm{ms}^{-2}$\) ( \(v\) is instantaneous velocity). Time taken by the car to come to rest is
questions.solution: Given, \(u=6.25 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$\) and \(a=-2.5 $\sqrt{v} \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$\), \(v=\) instantaneous velocity As we know, \$(a=\frac{d v}{d t}$\) So, \$(\frac{d v}{d t}=-$2.5 $\sqrt{v}$\) Integrate on the both sides, we get \(\begin{array}{llrl} \Rightarrow & \quad \int_{6.25}^0 $\frac{1}{\sqrt{v}}$d v & =-2.5 $\int$d t \\ \Rightarrow & {[2 $\sqrt{v}]_{6.25}^0}  \text{ and }  =-2.5 t \\ \Rightarrow  \text{ and }  t  \text{ and }  $=\frac{2 \times 2.5}{2.5}=$2 $\mathrm{~s} \end{array}\) Hence, the correct option is (a).
